attention_diagnostics.attention_coefficient_scale_formula: stored c~_r (static coefficients or query bias b) start at r! times the represented value; attention uses c_r = c~_r / r!
attention_diagnostics.attention_formula: sum_(i<=t) sum_(r<=8) c_r(x_t) s_ti^r v_i, s_ti = Q_t K_i^T / sqrt(d_k); c(x_t) = b + (a/r!)*tanh(x_t W) per layer/head, W initially N(0, 0.0334077^2) per entry, a initially 0, b_r initially 1/r!; x_t is the activation after the block input RMSNorm, then per-head RMSNorm over value channels with a learned gain; use this query polynomial h_t(s) for s>=0 and exp(s) h_t(s) for s<0; head RMSNorm evaluated on each token and head's output divided by its largest magnitude, a constant to differentiation, with its epsilon divided by that magnitude's square (an output too small for that keeps its plain evaluation): the same function, with an FP32 gradient that is exact to rounding wherever FP32 holds the gradient itself (its elements are of size cotangent / output RMS, and FP32's normal range ends at 1.2e-38)
attention_diagnostics.attention_score_formula: exp(gamma_h) * <RoPE(g_Q * q / sqrt(mean(q^2) + eps)), RoPE(g_K * k / sqrt(mean(k^2) + eps))> / sqrt(d_K); independent Q/K channel gains per layer, shared across heads; gamma_h learned independently per layer/head, initially zero
